problem_type: Context-sensitive MCP integration orchestration at a deterministic capability boundary
symptom: Agents are forced through discover/select/workflow-submit/input-resolution transitions that return opaque or provider-shaped failures for real-world relay APIs, including no-message validation failures and model-specific 500s.
direct_cause: The MCP integration surface exposes provider discovery and workflow orchestration as Nomi-owned transitions, while the deterministic persistence and certification boundaries are mixed into the same session API; invalid proposals are not rejected at one explicit, readable persistence gate.
class_root: The integration contract lacks a single fail-closed proposal boundary that accepts only public, already-prepared provider candidates/workflows and converges every write through owner + expectedRevision before persistence.
affected_population: MCP agents connecting HTTP providers, relays, or ComfyUI workflows
providers with non-canonical discovery, pagination, or workflow input conventions
all callers of the integration session MCP surface
entry_points: trusted UI integration session and catalog management callers
internal_only_reason: The missing invariant is an application-owned boundary; no third-party behavior decides whether a public proposal is safe to persist.
invariants: MCP integration input never contains API key, Authorization value, receipt token, or other credential value.
Every mutable integration session write checks owner and exact expectedRevision before any state or disk mutation.
A rejected proposal leaves session state and revision unchanged and returns a field-addressable repair reason.
Paid confirm and start remain separate receipt-authorized transitions.
Provider network configuration is encrypted at the catalog write boundary and proxy routing is per vendor connection.
generality_proof: Both HTTP candidate selection and ComfyUI workflow submission enter through the same propose action and IntegrationSessionService boundary; management updates and proxy toggles enter through the catalog's existing encrypted write boundary. Removing the four provider-shaped transitions prevents equivalent relay and workflow variance from re-entering through another MCP name, while preserving trusted UI callers where repository evidence shows shared use.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Validate the proposal shape and semantic relationship, then mutate the session only behind owner and expectedRevision CAS.
Execute the catalog JSON Schema at the MCP tools/call boundary, including additionalProperties rejection for credential-shaped fields.
Own persistent vendor/model management and reuse lineage, mapping, and catalog atomic write semantics.
Encrypt or explicitly clear per-vendor proxy configuration before catalog persistence.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: This is the replacement entry for both old HTTP select and Comfy workflow/input transitions; it dispatches only to the shared propose method.
These callers consume the proposal output but remain separately guarded by expectedRevision, signed receipt validation, and canonical certification run startup.
Renderer writes already converge on catalogStore and retain certification metadata protections; the management tool uses the same persistence owner.

recurrence.reason: Provider discovery and workflow conventions vary by vendor and can reproduce opaque failures through any future integration caller unless the deterministic persistence boundary is centralized.
same_class_scan: Searched integrationSession.ts, dispatcher.ts, mcpIntegrationTools.ts, and tests for begin/openCredentials/discover/select/submitWorkflow/resolveInput/requestConfirmation/start/cancel.
Checked rendererCatalogMutation.ts and catalogStore.ts for parallel vendor/model writes and networkConfigStore.ts/providerNetwork.ts for proxy routing consumers.
Checked MCP tools/call validation and L2 model-integration journeys for external entry points.

prevention.invariant: Only public, semantically valid candidates/workflows with exact owner and expectedRevision may reach persisted session state; management writes use catalog's encrypted atomic boundary.
prevention.failure_mode: Reject before mutation with a stable field path and repair instruction; unknown fields and credential-shaped fields fail the MCP tool call; paid transitions remain unavailable without the existing receipt seam.
prevention.strategy: Delete provider-shaped MCP transitions and route both proposal families through one validator/mutator, while reusing existing catalog encryption and lineage deletion instead of introducing parallel stores.

legacy_paths.rationale: The four provider-shaped MCP transitions are replaced by propose; trusted UI-only shared capabilities remain only if repository evidence requires them and are not exposed as MCP actions.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The repair owns an application boundary; no third-party dependency controls proposal validation, revision CAS, or catalog persistence.

migration: No persisted schema migration is required. Existing sessions remain readable; old MCP names/actions are removed from the catalog and callers must construct a public proposal. Existing catalog records retain their current encrypted network format.
residual_risks: A certification-owned vendor configuration change may still require the existing new-session policy; the final behavior must follow live main evidence and be reported if the management tool cannot safely apply it.
Real external provider variance remains intentionally delegated to the driving Agent and is not certified by the deterministic propose gate.
